title: Incipient superconductivity and tunable Chern insulators in twisted Bernal bilayer-trilayer graphene
authors: Derek Waleffe, Aryana Bhattacharyya, Manish Kumar, Eric Maginnis, Anna Okounkova, Tobias Faehndrich, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Joshua Folk, Matthew Yankowitz
abstract: Moiré superlattices assembled by twisting Bernal and rhombohedral multilayer graphene host a rich set of interaction-driven magnetic and topological states, yet superconductivity has not been observed in these systems except in proximity to a transition-metal dichalcogenide. Here we report incipient superconductivity and tunable Chern insulators in twisted Bernal bilayer-trilayer graphene encapsulated by hexagonal boron nitride. Across twist angles from $θ= 1.05^\circ$ to $1.50^\circ$, Chern insulators form at integer and fractional moiré fillings for electron doping, with Chern numbers up to |C| = 3 set by twist angle and tuned by doping. At $θ= 1.18^\circ$, a symmetry-broken metallic region forms for hole doping and hosts a trivial insulator at band filling $ν= -2$. Displacement field alone drives this insulator into a pocket of incipient superconductivity with a sharp transition, a well-defined critical current, and a critical temperature that peaks near the insulating boundary, although the resistance does not fall to zero. In-plane magnetic field expands the pocket, which persists to more than four times the weak-coupling Pauli limit, and stabilizes a second pocket in which Fraunhofer-like modulation of the critical current signals phase-coherent pairing. Twisted Bernal bilayer-trilayer graphene thus offers a single gate-tunable system in which pairing can be interfaced with Chern insulators whose topology is itself an adjustable parameter.
summary: This work reports on the discovery of incipient superconductivity and tunable Chern insulators in twisted Bernal bilayer-trilayer graphene. By controlling the twist angle and doping, the system allows for the precise tuning of topological invariants and the emergence of superconducting pairing. This makes the material a highly versatile platform for studying correlated electronic phenomena.
main_problem: The study investigates the emergence of superconductivity and tunable Chern insulating states in twisted Bernal bilayer-trilayer graphene.
main_result: The authors report observing incipient superconductivity, characterized by a low-resistance pocket, and tunable Chern insulators in this single, gate-controllable van der Waals system.
method: Transport measurements ($ho_{xx}, ho_{xy}$) are performed using dual-gated Hall bar devices across varying twist angles and doping levels, supplemented by Landau fan analysis.
model_or_system: The physical platform is twisted Bernal bilayer-trilayer graphene encapsulated by hBN, forming moiré superlattices. The system's electronic properties are controlled by tuning the twist angle ($	heta$) and the carrier density/displacement field ($D$).
key_observables: Chern numbers ($|C|$), critical temperature ($T_c$), critical current ($I_c$), and longitudinal/Hall resistivity ($ho_{xx}, ho_{xy}$).
important_parameters:
Twist angles ($	heta \approx 1.05^\circ$ to $1.50^\circ$), moiré filling factor ($
u$), and in-plane magnetic field ($B_{\parallel}$).
main_assumptions: The superconductivity observed is described as 'incipient' because the resistance does not fully drop to zero, and the analysis relies on gate-tunability to control topology.
figures_summary: Figures map out $ho_{xx}$ and $ho_{xy}$ across doping/displacement fields, showing Chern insulator plateaus and superconducting dome structures, with additional figures detailing the field dependence of these features.
paper_structure:
The paper systematically maps out the phase diagram by varying twist angle and doping, first identifying Chern insulator states, then observing the correlated insulator at $
u=-2$, and finally detailing the superconducting pocket and its response to magnetic fields.
why_interesting: The ability to interface tunable topological states (Chern insulators) directly with superconducting pairing in a single, gate-tunable 2D material platform is highly relevant for realizing novel quantum electronic devices.
